issues.required_property: Each finite corrective test run referenced by the execution contract has an explicit executable command, a separately captured result, and a defined success condition.
issues.description: The execution contract allocates Task 1 GREEN, up to one diagnosed correction plus final GREEN, Task 2 RED/GREEN/correction/final GREEN, and Task 3 correction recovery slots, but the task verification elements specify only Task 1 baseline RED and first GREEN groups, Task 2 RED and first GREEN groups, and Task 3 full suite/validators/review. No command or acceptance condition invokes the named correction groups or Task 3's six-test recovery group. If a first GREEN fails, the plan says to run a correction and final check, but the executor has no exact command or asserted outcome for those reserved slots.
issues.fix_hint: Make every reserved correction/recovery slot executable and state how its captured exit/native result determines whether the next slot may run.

issues.required_property: A task's automated verification path must recognize its explicitly required expected RED result as successful evidence while still failing on an unintended result.
issues.description: Task 1 requires its first automated command to exit 1 with one native failure as the mandatory pre-edit RED, and Task 2 similarly requires a two-test failing RED. Those commands appear as ordinary <automated> verifications in the task, while the plan specifies expected output under <fails_when> and does not define a wrapper or evidence consumer that converts only the exact expected RED into a successful verification result. As written, a runner treating automated-command nonzero exits as task failure will halt before GREEN, or a runner requiring the command to pass will reject the intended RED.
issues.fix_hint: Define an executable capture/check path that preserves the raw nonzero invocation and returns success only when the exact expected RED signature, source identity, and capture requirements match; apply the same rule to Task 2's expected RED.

issues.required_property: An unresolved phase requirement or decision remains clearly identified as unresolved and is not represented as satisfied by the plan.
issues.description: The plan explicitly says CIREL-01's unclassified edge remains unresolved and keeps the requirement partial_not_reproduced, while the roadmap requires either reproduced/fixed selected failures or an adequately supported no-flake path before completion. This is an honest scope boundary for this gap-repair plan, not evidence that the phase requirement is complete; retain it as open through later plans and phase verification.
issues.fix_hint: Keep CIREL-01 open and make the downstream reproduction or supported no-flake disposition an explicit prerequisite to phase acceptance.
